descriptionChirho: A horse, the domesticated equine animal; in the NT used predominantly in Revelation's apocalyptic visions (the four horsemen, cavalry of 200 million, horses with lion heads), and in James 3:3 as an illustration of controlling the tongue with a bit. Multilingual evidence confirms singular and plural as the same concept: Spanish 'caballo/caballos', Hindi 'ghora/ghoron', Arabic 'hisanun/khaylin', Korean 'mal/maldeul', Swahili 'farasi'. The plural forms (N-GMP, N-DMP, N-AMP) and singular forms (N-NMS, N-GMS) represent grammatical number inflection of one unified sense referring to the same animal.
